tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

Done. Here's a summary of the payment:

**Payment Report — Evergreen Catering**

- **Invoice:** INV-53113 (approved, due 2026-11-04)
- **Amount paid:** $3,082.44
- **Rail:** Wire (Evergreen Catering supports wire, so no ACH fallback was needed)
- **Payment ID:** PAY0001
- **Status:** Sent — invoice marked paid in full

**Notes:**
- My first wire attempt for the full original amount ($3,350.48) was rejected — not executed — because the invoice balance had been reduced by credit memo CM-3113 (-$268.04). The payment was then made for the correct outstanding balance, so nothing was overpaid or double-paid.
- The payment was sent with an idempotency key, guaranteeing it executes exactly once.
- The other two Evergreen invoices were untouched: INV-10314 is already paid, and INV-21757 is still a draft awaiting approval.
- No controller approval was required since the payment is under the $10,000 threshold.
